title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: In one-hot encoding, each category is represented by a binary vector. For the $$job_{type}$$ variable, we have three categories: blue collar, white collar, and managerial. How would you represent a white collar worker using one-hot encoding?

title: Substitute Values into the Model
text: Once you have the one-hot encoded values for a white collar worker, substitute them into the model equation: $$y=-8+3x_{edu}+6x_m-3x_b$$. Remember, $$x_{edu}$$ is the years of education.

title: Calculate the Predicted Wage
text: For a white collar worker with $$10$$ years of education, substitute the values into the equation: $$y=-8+3\times10+6\times0-3\times0$$. What is the predicted wage?
